h1: Pipe and tube benders — CNC, NC mandrel, hydraulic and rotary draw
intro: A pipe bender or tube bending machine draws a tube around a bend die to a set angle; a mandrel bender adds an internal mandrel so thin-wall tube bends to a tight radius without wrinkling or collapsing. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, each on its own page: CNC tube benders that feed, rotate and bend from a program — CSM all-electric, electric-hybrid and hydraulic CNC mandrel benders from Ø15/32″ to Ø8-5/8″ and ISITAN SFB 3- and 5-axis servo CNC benders to Ø3-1/2″; NC mandrel benders with programmed bend angles — ISITAN SFB NC, NC/C, compact and aluminum-profile benders and CSM symmetric, TSRJ / TDRJ, TNCPB and TNCB NC benders to Ø8-5/8″ pipe; and hydraulic and rotary draw pipe benders without a mandrel — ISITAN BK, the premium-line TB and SPB benders and NovoTech's value-line hydraulic, electric and air-hydraulic benders to Ø3-1/8″. From a bench bender for 1″ pipe to a 20 ft hydraulic CNC pipe bender for shipyard pipe, every machine is supplied with installation and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. Below, each page in brief and every model in one capacity table.

range_note: Tube capacities are for mild steel; stainless, aluminum, bar and box-section capacities for the BK series are on the hydraulic and rotary draw page. CLR = centreline radius (the largest die radius). Working length is the maximum feed with the standard mandrel rod (extended mandrels to 20 ft are optional on SFB models); for the CSM symmetric benders it is the span between the two bends. Weights for the CSM benders are quoted with the configuration.

faq.q: Pipe bender, tube bender, mandrel bender — what is the difference?
faq.a: "Pipe" is sized by nominal pipe size (NPS) and schedule, "tube" by outside diameter and wall, but the machines are the same: a bend die, a clamp and a pressure die draw the material around the radius. A mandrel bender adds an internal mandrel so thin-wall tube can be bent to a tight radius without wrinkling; the CNC and NC benders on these pages are mandrel benders, the BK, TB, SPB and value-line benders bend without a mandrel. Every capacity on these pages is given as OD × wall in inches and gauge.

faq.q: How do I choose a tube bender?
faq.a: Start with the largest tube (OD × wall and material), the tightest centreline radius and the number of bends per part — that sets mandrel or not and the model size. Then the volume: a hydraulic or rotary draw bender for occasional bends, an NC mandrel bender for programmed angles with manual feed, a carrier or servo-feed NC for repeatable multi-plane parts, and a CNC when parts come from a drawing in hundreds. Send us a part drawing and we will size the machine and tooling.

faq.q: Which tube benders does NovoTech stock?
faq.a: We keep the SFB 38-NC and 51-NC and the BK-050 in Mississauga, ON, Canada, and bring CNC models, carrier models and the larger 76 and 90 sizes in to order with their tooling. In-stock machines carry the 7-day money-back guarantee. CSM benders are quoted with the tooling for your part drawings.

Both are mandrel benders sold, installed and supported by NovoTech. The ISITAN SFB benders (Turkey) cover Ø1-1/4″ to Ø3-1/2″ with NC and CNC models for the job shop and fabricator. CSM covers a far wider range — from Ø15/32″ brake line to Ø8-5/8″ pipe — with all-electric and hybrid machines, stacked tools, boosters and automation for series production. Send us the part drawing and the tube and we quote the right machine from either range.

faq.q: Do you install tube benders and train operators?
faq.a: Yes — our technicians commission the bender anywhere in Canada, set up the first tooling, prove out your part and train operators on the NC or CNC. Remote assistance over the network is built into the CNC models, and we support every machine by video call.

faq.q: What do you need from me to quote tooling?
faq.a: Six things: material type, tube or profile size, wall thickness, the smallest centreline radius (CLR) you bend, the maximum bend angle and the maximum tube length. Every bender comes with one die set in the size you request; extra sets, ball mandrels and wiper dies are quoted from the same list.

faq.q: What voltage do the benders run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.
